title: Community summaries (GraphRAG-style aggregation)
keyFindings: Community summaries (Microsoft GraphRAG global search) answer global/theme-level questions that vector-only retrieval cannot, but are the most expensive part of GraphRAG: an LLM summary pass over every community at every hierarchy level, paid at index time.

LightRAG deliberately skips the community-summarization pass and reports matching/beating GraphRAG on retrieval accuracy at roughly 1-2 orders of magnitude lower token cost (up to ~100x), demonstrating the pass is optional, not core.

The suite's primary graph is a sparse reference graph (fact/reference/link/embed, astrographer.md §4.2), not a dense entity graph, so full Leiden hierarchical community detection is mis-shaped for Astrographer; Zodiac's pre-graphed dependency graph is the one dense-entity fit.

Astrographer has no community-summary contract element: getConsistencyReport (§4.2.3) is per-reference, not a summary, and ragQuery/ragStream (§4.3.2) return flat top-K results with no global/theme mode.

A scoped, lazy, local community-summary surface (Astrographer wiki-level/document-cluster, Zodiac per-target, Astral published-wiki) is D2-compatible and answers the source talk's global-question gap without the index-time cost cliff.
The full Microsoft GraphRAG hierarchical community-summarization pipeline stays PARKED for D2 cost/latency reasons; the scoped wiki-level/per-target summary is the SHOULD expression.
summary: Community summaries (GraphRAG global search) enable theme-level questions but are the most expensive part of GraphRAG; LightRAG's evidence shows the full hierarchical summarization pass is optional. For the suite, a scoped, lazy, local community-summary surface (Astrographer wiki-level/document-cluster, Zodiac per-target, Astral published-wiki) is a SHOULD that closes the global-question gap at acceptable D2 cost and is exposable on both GUI and MCP (D4); the full hierarchical pipeline stays PARKED.
